title: Summed products of positive tag features and payloads, divided by a summed tag total on reading
summary: A reader of the probe's positive features is divided by the same features applied to a running total of all earlier tag features, so what comes out is a weighted average of earlier payloads. To make this possible every symbol adds the product of its positive tag features and its payload vector to a square accumulator and adds the tag features to a total.
core_idea: Accumulate tag-feature times payload products and a tag-feature total, then read both with the probe's positive features so the output is a weighted average of earlier payloads.

state.name: A
state.meaning: Accumulator: for every earlier position, the product of its positive tag features (length r) and its payload (length d), summed.

state.name: n_tot
state.meaning: Total of the positive tag features of every earlier position; it divides the reading.

update.name: total
update.plain: nu_t = nu_(t-1) + g_t, the total n_tot after symbol t

update.name: tag and payload
update.plain: g_t = psi(U_g h_t) and p_t = U_p h_t, with h_t = Emb[s_t] the embedding of the current symbol s_t and psi(s) = elu(s) + 1 applied elementwise, which keeps every feature positive

readout.name: prediction
readout.plain: the scores Z o_t over the V symbols; the next symbol is their argmax

readout.name: probe reading
readout.plain: f_t = psi(U_f h_t) are the probe features; o_t = A_t^T f_t / (nu_t . f_t), the normalized reading

learning.description: All projection matrices and offsets are fitted by gradient descent on the cross-entropy of the following symbol over a training corpus, with backpropagation through the full sequence.
learning.few_shot_argument: Nothing in the design helps with few examples; recall of 4 pairs takes about 3200 training sequences.

complexity.total_sequence: Theta(n r d + n d V)
complexity.constants_notes: Per symbol one rank-one addition to an r by d accumulator, one r by d reading and the d by V output map. Accumulator and total hold r d + r numbers whatever the length.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Gradient descent; nothing in the design helps with few examples.

prediction.statement: Starting from random weights, 3200 training sequences of 4 pairs over 16 symbols reach recall accuracy 0.99.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: With hand-set position features, strings of length L <= r are copied exactly; longer strings blur together in the accumulator.
With hand-set weights and K mutually orthogonal tag feature vectors (so K <= r), recall is exact; past r pairs the reading blends payloads.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: The operation count of a reference implementation grows faster than linearly in n with r, d and V fixed.
Some hand-set configuration of an r by d accumulator recalls more than r pairs exactly.

toy_example.description: A two by two accumulator after two symbols, read with one probe.
toy_example.python:
import json, math
def psi(s):
    return [v + 1.0 if v > 0 else math.exp(v) for v in s]
A = [[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]]
tot = [0.0, 0.0]
for raw, pay in [([1.0, -0.5], [2.0, 1.0]), ([-1.0, 0.5], [0.0, 3.0])]:
    g = psi(raw)
    for i in range(2):
        tot[i] += g[i]
        for j in range(2):
            A[i][j] += g[i] * pay[j]
f = psi([0.5, 0.5])
den = sum(tot[i] * f[i] for i in range(2))
o = [sum(A[i][j] * f[i] for i in range(2)) / den for j in range(2)]
print(json.dumps({"reading": [round(v, 6) for v in o], "total": [round(v, 6) for v in tot]}))
